title: Good Debt vs. Bad Debt: How the Rich Use Leverage to Build Wealth
summary: Rich Dad blog post defining good debt by the cash-flow test and arguing leverage plus other people's money multiplies real estate returns.

assertions.quote: bad debt takes money out of your pocket every month, and good debt puts money into it

verdicts.note: A definitional framing rather than a testable claim.

assertions.quote: the more of a deal financed with OPM, the higher the return on the capital an investor does put in
Even cash-flowing debt carries risk — vacancy, rate changes, market shifts

verdicts.note: Leveraged real estate investors were wiped out in 2008; the symmetry of leverage is arithmetic.

assertions.quote: A personal residence is a liability rather than an asset, because it doesn’t generate income
one of the sharper financial-education gaps separating the E and S quadrants from the B and I quadrants
she can refinance, return investor capital, and keep the cash flow indefinitely: an infinite return

verdicts.note: Possible when rents and appreciation support a cash-out refinance, but the larger loan cuts cash flow and raises risk.

assertions.quote: takes roughly 23 years to pay off and costs about $7,723 in interest — more than the original balance itself

verdicts.note: Standard amortization at 20% APR with minimum payments produces this result.

assertions.quote: Track record and financial intelligence attract capital more reliably than having capital in the first place.

verdicts.note: Syndicators do raise outside money, but a track record usually requires capital to build first.
